prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized game asset.
Edit the door artwork in image 1 using image 2 as the EXACT FRONT-ELEVATION SILHOUETTE TEMPLATE. Output ONE finished ARCHED WOODEN DOOR LEAF, straight-on, on a genuinely transparent background.
The previous rectangular painted panel was rejected. Repaint it as an actual arched door from the beginning: the outermost wood, the cut ends of its vertical boards, highlights, worn bevel and edge shading must all FOLLOW the rounded upper arch in image 2. No straight horizontal top edge and no rectangular top corners. Follow the squat rounded silhouette in image 2: width/total height about .907, upper semicircle above straight vertical sides, flat bottom. Do NOT add a stone frame or a second decorative arch.
Keep image 1's illustrated dark-fantasy hand-painted style, dark warm wood, forged blue-black iron, one purple inset and the substantial ring handle. Broad stylized facets and readable details, not photorealistic. Keep the entire silhouette within the square canvas with transparent margins like image 2; do not crop it.
SECOND REQUIRED CORRECTION: both horizontal iron straps are significantly SHORTER and comfortably inset into the wood. Their extremities, including pointed ends and end rivets, must be at 20% and 80% of the door's total width, leaving a very obvious broad strip of exposed wood on BOTH sides. Use fewer rivets if necessary. Place upper strap near 42% of door height, lower strap near 81%. Leave clear wood below the bottom strap. All ironwork must remain well inside the arched silhouette, with no touches at its edges.
Keep a single modest purple diamond inset at the middle of the upper strap. Its violet glow is localized. Keep one ring handle on the right between the straps, centered around 65% of leaf width and 63% height, slightly moved inward from image 1; comfortable clear wood around its mounting plate. Readability at 100 pixels wide matters. Preserve the crafted attachment shadows and subdued metal highlights.
No scene, no floor, no torches, no stone, no text, no guides, no checkerboard drawn into the image. True native alpha outside the wooden leaf. Image 2's silhouette is the shape constraint; image 1 supplies the artwork style only.

Edit image 1, the arched wooden door sprite. Keep its style, wood colors, arched wooden top, rim, localized violet seal, ring handle, transparent background, and no stone frame.
REQUIRED change: SHORTEN BOTH IRON STRAPS MUCH MORE. Their overall horizontal width INCLUDING their wide end caps must be only 58% of the wooden leaf's width. Currently the end caps are at roughly 10% and 90% of the leaf; move them inward to 21% and 79%. Leave a full exposed plank-width of wood on the LEFT AND RIGHT of each strap. You may reduce the upper strap to two end rivets total, one at each end, plus the central violet inset. No need to fit four rivets. Keep the metal substantial in height, not thin.
Also match the wider, less tall leaf silhouette of image 2 exactly (width/height .907, top semicircle, straight sides and flat bottom). Preserve continuous hand-painted worn wood bevels along the ROUND arch, no straight horizontal top.
The big ring remains between the two straps on the right but comfortably inside their ends. All hardware must feel set well INSIDE the wooden area. One single-leaf door. Straight-on elevation, no visible depth or perspective.
Output one complete native-alpha sprite on transparent background, no extra shadow outside the silhouette, no text, no labels, no floor or room. Image 2 is only a shape template; do not copy its flat colors.
scope: Arched painting and shorter inset straps; same approved v8 geometry.
